item.title: Southern California Utilities Prep Shutoffs as Fire Risk Surges
item.description: Thousands of homes and businesses in Southern California have been warned of the potential for power cuts in the coming days as a heat wave boosts wildfire risk throughout the region. With triple-digit temperatures expected this weekend, Edison International’s Southern California utility said it is mulling preventive power shutoffs Friday and Saturday for 9,990 customers in Riverside County, south of San Bernardino National Forest. has also flagged potential shutoffs for more than 35,000 customers in “at-risk communities” near mountain foothills.

item.title: Firms’ confidence, satisfaction and trust in the FCA rise
item.description: The latest FCA and Practitioner Panel survey shows rising levels of satisfaction, confidence and trust in the FCA among firms, alongside a strong understanding of Consumer Duty expectations. The proportion of firms rating the FCA as a highly effective regulator also increased from 69% to 76%, while 75% reported high levels of trust. There was a 27-percentage point increase in firms’ understanding of the Secondary International Competitiveness and Growth Objective and a 25-percentage point increase in confidence in our delivery of it.

item.title: Reporter’s Notebook: Europe’s Sovereign AI Push Needs Customers As Well As Capital
item.description: Europe’s AI startups are attracting record sums, but funding alone won’t give the region more control over its AI future. That investment surge is sharpening a question at the heart of the sovereign AI debate: Where should countries concentrate their resources to capture the technology’s economic value and retain control over their data? Their perspectives from Europe and the United Arab Emirates, respectively, pointed to opportunities in specialized chips and applications and underscored how purchasing decisions, government mandates and access to computing power can determine whether AI ambitions translate into growth.

item.title: Nautical And Marine Startups See Stepped-Up Funding
item.description: Considering that more than 70% of Earth’s surface is covered by water, one might expect nautical- and marine-focused startups would capture more than just a pittance of venture investment. Over the past year, venture backers have poured close to $3 billion into good-sized rounds for marine-related startups in sectors ranging from defense tech to clean energy, per Crunchbase data. Navy as a key customer, secured $1.75 billion in Series D funding in March.

item.title: Your Investors Can Make Or Break Your Startup. Here’s Who Founders Actually Need On Their Cap Table
item.description: Here’s what founders should look for in their investors. Founders have to seek out strategic investors: People or institutions with industry expertise, relationships and resources that can help founders solve problems capital alone cannot. For founders raising venture capital, the instinct is often to get the money, as much and as quickly as possible.

item.title: NA commercial property insurance rates fall the most in a decade, hard market reverses: Willis
item.description: The North America commercial property insurance market has experienced its sharpest decline in rates a decade, according to broker Willis, with wide-spread double-digit price reductions for clients as the soft market ensues and “the multi-year hard market fully reverses.” Abundant capacity is weighing on property insurance and in large and complex accounts softening has been seen across all program types, the Willis (a WTW business) Insurance Marketplace Realities report makes clear. Property rates also continue to soften in the middle-market, where secondary peril exposure and risk discipline are shaping outcomes, Willis explained. The broker reports that rates for large and complex property insurance programs fell by an average of 14.5% in the second quarter of 2026, an acceleration from 8.4% in the prior year, while shared and layered placements fell further with rates down 23.41%, again accelerated from 14.57% in Q2 2025.

item.title: Hannover Re Capital Partners establishes new Bermuda fund structure and SPI
item.description: Hannover Re Capital Partners, the Bermuda-based insurance-linked securities (ILS) platform established by global reinsurance firm Hannover Re, is continuing to expand its activities on the island, with new fund infrastructure established to support ILS investment options for clients. But with this new ILS fund structure and SPI now registered, it suggests the Hannover Re Capital Partners unit could raise fresh capital and have more to deploy in 2027. First, Hannover Re Capital Partners Fund Ltd.

item.title: Willis reports sharp fall in North American property insurance rates
item.description: Willis, the insurance brokerage and risk advisory business of WTW, has released its autumn 2026 Insurance Marketplace Realities report, The Specialist View: Navigating Tomorrow’s Risk Landscape for 2027, r eporting that rates for large and complex property risks fell by an average of 14.5% during the second quarter of 2026, compared with an 8.4% reduction during the same period in 2025. Casualty insurance is showing different conditions to the property market, according to Willis. According to Willis, property market conditions have continued to move away from the hard market experienced between 2018 and 2024, with pricing approaching levels last seen in 2019.

item.title: Paragon strengthens Specialty Property leadership team with new promotions
item.description: These appointments strengthen Paragon’s Specialty Property leadership team and support continued growth across the organisation. These promotions highlight Paragon’s investment in its Specialty Property business and its leadership, and demonstrate its commitment to internal talent development, enhancing the underwriting expertise, capabilities, and service provided to retail agent and carrier partners. Promoted to executive vice president of Paragon Insurance Holdings, Denton will continue collaborating with the Specialty Property team while spearheading strategic initiatives across the broader organisation.

item.title: Lincoln closes $6.3bn reinsurance transaction with Talcott
item.description: Lincoln Financial has closed its previously announced $6.3 billion reinsurance transaction with Talcott Financial Group, effective October 1, 2026. Lincoln explained that the $6.3 billion total transaction includes the reinsurance by a Talcott subsidiary of approximately $5.8 billion of in-force guaranteed universal life (GUL) statutory reserves , representing approximately 37% of Lincoln’s remaining in-force GUL block. Combined with Lincoln’s 2023 reinsurance transaction with Fortitude Re, approximately 60% of Lincoln’s total GUL block is now reinsured, which further reduces Lincoln’s exposure to a legacy, capital-intensive block of business.

item.title: International Criminal Court, AXA Cut Ties Amid Trump Campaign Against Court
item.description: President Donald Trump recently urged other countries to leave the ICC, calling it “evil” and “a rogue institution,” amid an escalating US campaign against the court. The International Criminal Court has ended its contract with French life and health insurer AXA starting October 1 and will now be using a new health insurance provider , a spokesperson for the Hague-based court said . The Trump administration says the ICC oversteps its authority by claiming jurisdiction over citizens of countries, including the United States and Israel, which have not ratified the court’s founding treaty, known as the Rome Statute.

item.title: US States Challenge Corteva Spinoff as Bid to Evade PFAS Liabilities
item.description: Fifteen US states sued a grichemicals company Corteva on Thursday, alleging that the spinoff of its seed and genetics business into Vylor was designed to shield the company’s best assets from tens of billions of dollars in potential liabilities tied to PFAS “forever chemicals” that have polluted the environment. The states allege that the Vylor spinoff transferred one of Corteva’s most profitable businesses to a new company while leaving PFAS liabilities behind, amounting to an effort to defraud creditors pursuing claims against former DuPont entities. Corteva said in September that the states’ PFAS claims are “speculative and unproven,” adding that Corteva itself never made or sold PFAS products.

item.title: Police Arrest Dual UK-Iranian National Over Airbase Plot
item.description: UK police said they arrested a sixth man, a British-Iranian dual national, in relation to an incident near an airbase used by the US to launch strikes on Iran. “We’re looking at all possible angles – including possible foreign state involvement.” Five men were arrested on Sunday night over the incident near the RAF Fairford airbase. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday that the UK believed there was Iranian state involvement in the plot.

item.title: Samsung insurance affiliates join $1 billion Helix investment
item.description: Samsung Life Insurance and Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance are among six Samsung affiliates investing a combined $1 billion in Helix Digital Infrastructure , an AI infrastructure company established by KKR. The Samsung affiliates’ investment in Helix extends that pattern to a company pursuing data centers, power and network infrastructure together. Samsung said the investment could create opportunities for its affiliates across semiconductors, data center construction, cooling systems, IT services and backup power.

item.title: Asurion expands LeakProtect with monitoring-only option
item.description: Asurion has added LeakProtect Essential to its managed water loss prevention program for insurance carriers, expanding its offering to homes where installing an automatic shutoff valve may not be practical or necessary. LeakProtect Standard already uses Phyn Plus, its whole-home monitoring and automatic shutoff system. With LeakProtect Essential, we’re bringing that same approach to even more homes.” – Rob Sader, VP and GM of Asurion LeakProtect.

item.title: KYND Adds AI Detection for Cyber Underwriting
item.description: (Image source:KYND website.) KYND (Austin, Texas) has launched an AI discovery capability designed to help cyber insurers identify AI technologies across an organization’s external digital footprint during risk selection. “If the same AI technologies and dependencies are showing up repeatedly across insureds, that can quickly become an accumulation issue.” KYND says the capability builds on its broader technology-detection platform, which also identifies services and tools including payment and cloud platforms, analytics and tracking pixels, session-recording technology, identity and access management systems and website infrastructure. The capability works from a single domain and does not require information supplied directly by the insured, giving underwriters an independently observed source of data to use alongside proposal forms and underwriting discussions.

item.title: bolttech, Bold Penguin Form Global Distribution Alliance
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) bolttech (Singapore) and Bold Penguin (Dublin, Ohio) have formed a global strategic alliance to develop a combined commercial and personal lines insurance distribution offering for agents, insurers and embedded distribution partners in the U.S., Europe and Asia. The companies say the arrangement will combine Bold Penguin’s commercial lines distribution technology and carrier network with bolttech’s personal lines capabilities, AI-enabled workflows and international insurance distribution infrastructure. For Bold Penguin, the alliance provides a route to expand its commercial lines capabilities internationally while adding bolttech personal lines offerings for its U.S.

item.title: EU’s Insurance Watchdog Warns of Risks Tied to Extreme Heat
item.description: Europe’s insurance and pensions watchdog warned extreme heat is adding to the risks the two industries face. “Our preliminary study shows that it could become a material risk factor for certain insurance lines and pension providers, despite offsetting factors and strong diversification across products and risks.” The warning is the latest by EU authorities charged with safeguarding the bloc’s economic stability. The credit ratings company said that while the recent wildfires are unlikely to significantly affect scores, more frequent extreme weather events risk undermining “the resilience, insurability, liquidity, and valuation of certain assets and borrowers.” It urged lenders to check the extent to which potential losses can be mitigated through insurance and other instruments.

item.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain Retires X2 Roller Coaster Amid Brain Injury Lawsuits
item.description: Six Flags Magic Mountain said Tuesday that it is retiring its famous X2 roller coaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride. According to the Six Flags Magic Mountain website, the X2 roller coaster reaches a top speed of 76 mph (122 kph) and has a total length of 3,610 feet (1,100 meters). Six Flags recently settled a wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022, and three more lawsuits alleging traumatic brain injuries were filed last week.

item.title: AI Tech Execs Sign Voluntary Safety Pact, Back Data Center Expansion
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said tech executives agreed to establish voluntary standards for AI and reiterated his support for rapid expansion of data centers, as concerns mount over AI safety and the industry’s growing footprint in communities. Asked whether he was concerned that his support for data centers could hurt Republicans in November, Trump said tech companies would work to make communities “happy” about the construction of data centers. Trump made the comments after meeting with tech executives at the White House.

item.title: Vehicle Theft Continue to Drop, Down 21% in First Half of 2026
item.description: Newly released data shows that all 50 states have recorded year-over-year percentage decreases in vehicle thefts during the first half of 2026, according to the National Insurance Crime Bureau (NICB). The Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim, California metro area recorded the highest number of vehicle thefts during the first half of 2026, with 21,540 vehicles stolen. A total of 268,415 vehicle thefts were reported to law enforcement during the first six months of 2026, the NICB reported.

item.title: Exclusive: Homeward Raises $120M To Help Homeowners Buy And Sell More Quickly As Housing Market Stalls
item.description: “We realized that there’s an opportunity to help homeowners sell their home fast without sacrificing all of their home equity like they would have to if they sold to an investor,” founder and CEO Tim Heyl told Crunchbase News in an interview. Homeward , a startup that helps homeowners buy before selling their existing homes or get cash offers for their properties, has raised a $120 million Series D round, Crunchbase News reports exclusively. The company declined to disclose the valuation at which it raised the latest round, saying it was similar to its valuation at the time of its $136 million Series C raise in 2021, when it was reported to be “just north of $800 million.” Austin-based Homeward has also secured a $330 million asset-backed debt facility to fund more home transactions.

item.title: For ILS, attracting capital is not the challenge, it’s creating new opportunities to deploy: LGT’s Paul
item.description: Whilst the ILS market has consistently managed to deliver strong growth throughout recent years, a number of challenges still hinder across the industry, however Paul indicates that attracting capital is not one of them, but rather, finding opportunities to absorb it. “Contrary to popular belief, the challenge is not attracting capital. The real question is thus whether the industry can find attractive and scalable risk opportunities to absorb this additional capital, while maintaining adequate returns for all investors,” Paul told Artemis.

item.title: Bermuda marks 10 years of Solvency II equivalence amid €229.5bn EEA reinsurance market
item.description: Bermuda is marking a decade of Solvency II equivalence with Ten Years of Solvency II Equivalence , a new report produced by the Association of Bermuda Insurers and Reinsurers (ABIR), which represents Bermuda’s commercial insurance and reinsurance sector, in partnership with the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) and the European Capital Markets Institute (ECMI), examining the role of Bermuda’s commercial reinsurance market in providing risk-bearing capacity to European insurers. The report comes as Bermuda marks 10 years since it secured full Solvency II equivalence on 1 January 2016. For the European reinsurance market, the report examines the significance of Solvency II equivalence beyond Bermuda itself, focusing on its implications for insurers across the European Economic Area (EEA) and, in particular, the region’s access to international risk-bearing capacity.

item.title: VIPR names Tom Boucher as Non-Executive Chair as company enters next growth phase
item.description: VIPR Solutions, a specialist insurance technology company providing software and data solutions for the Delegated Authority market, has appointed Tom Boucher as its new Non-Executive Chair following Bridgepoint Growth’s investment in the business. “I’ve spent much of my career in specialty insurance software, and I’m excited to work with Paul, the management team and Bridgepoint to build on what VIPR has achieved.” Boucher’s appointment follows Bridgepoint Growth’s investment in the company and comes as the business focuses on expanding into additional markets while continuing to develop its technology offering. Boucher will work with VIPR Co-Founder and CEO Paul Templar and the company’s management team as VIPR continues to expand its international presence, enhance its artificial intelligence capabilities and improve the speed and simplicity of adopting its platform.

item.title: Everest ‘further sharpens’ its portfolio as sale of Canadian Retail Insurance arm completes
item.description: Everest Group, a global specialty reinsurer and insurer, has completed the sale of its Canadian Retail Insurance operations, Everest Insurance Company of Canada (Everest Canada), to The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company. “The completion of this transaction further sharpens Everest’s portfolio and positions the Company to concentrate its capital and capabilities on its core Reinsurance and Global Wholesale and Specialty Insurance businesses,” said Jim Williamson, Everest President and CEO. This transaction marks another move in Everest’s strategic repositioning and advances the carrier’s previously announced plan to exit the Commercial Retail Insurance space, following the 2025 sale of its global Retail Commercial Insurance renewal rights to AIG .

item.title: People Moves: AIG Names Hussain CRO for Retiring Schaper
item.description: Hussain succeeds Christopher Schaper as CRO. American International Group (AIG) said Turab Hussain was appointed executive vice president and c hief risk officer of AIG, effective Oct. Hussain will report to Eric Andersen , president & CEOr, AIG and will serve on AIG’s Executive Leadership Team.

item.title: Allianz Appoints Kroetz and Floquet as CEOs at Allianz Partners and Allianz Direct
item.description: Laurent Floquet , currently chief operating officer of Allianz Partners, will succeed Kroetz as CEO of Allianz Direct, bringing deep expertise in mobility and service-led customer solutions to his new role. Philipp Kroetz , currently chief executive officer of Allianz Direct, will become CEO of Allianz Partners, effective Nov. Allianz Group announced chief executive officer appointments at Allianz Partners and Allianz Direct, following Tomas Kunzmann’s appointment to the Allianz SE Board of Management.

item.title: Florida Commissioner Suspends A-Cap’s Atlantic Coast Life Over Surplus Issues
item.description: Two weeks after South Carolina’s insurance regulator took steps to place Atlantic Coast Life Insurance into rehabilitation, another state’s commissioner has suspended the company amid concerns about its finances. “In making the decision to suspend Atlantic Coast’s COA (certificate of authority), the Office determined that Atlantic Coast is impaired and that another insurance supervisory official, namely the South Carolina Department of Insurance, initiated rehabilitation proceedings…” reads a final order from Florida Commissioner Michael Yaworsky, signed Wednesday, Sept. Atlantic Coast Life is domiciled in South Carolina but was authorized to do business in Florida in 2006 as a life and health insurer.

item.title: Is Corgi getting into banking?
item.description: Corgi hasn’t announced any banking plans, but the company often describes itself as an “AI financial infrastructure company.” Getting a bank charter from scratch is a difficult, expensive, and time-consuming process. Based on information obtained by Coverager, it appears that insurance startup Corgi is working on a banking offering. A public documentation site at docs.dev.bank.corgi.com , which needs no login, describes the Corgi Bank API, a core banking system covering checking and savings accounts, debit cards and ATMs, ACH, wires and instant payments, business loans, and mortgages.

item.title: CBC Underwriters files ABCover school insurance trademark
item.description: CBC Underwriters has filed a trademark application for ABCover, an insurance brand focused on school districts. The company says its coverage is backed by the global insurance market, including underwriters at Lloyd’s of London. The trademark application, filed September 17, covers insurance agency services, property and casualty underwriting, and insurance consulting.

item.title: The Zebra welcomes Muse
item.description: Insurance comparison site The Zebra announced that it will offer agent-to-agent integration with AI personal assistant Muse. The integration with Muse, and other AI assistants in the future, will allow personal assistants to extract relevant policy details and declaration pages directly from connected user documents and hand them off to The Zebra’s agent harness. With Muse, instead of searching for documents and entering the same information again and again, they can share their details with The Zebra once and go directly to personalized comparison results.” – Daniel Herrington, chief AI officer at The Zebra.

item.title: Outmarket in California AI Raises $34.5M Series B
item.description: San Francisco-based Outmarket AI announced it has raised $34.5 million in Series B funding. The funding comes months after the company announced a $17 million Series A. The latest round brings Outmarket’s total funding to $56.5 million.

item.title: AI Safety Measures Widely Backed by Most Americans, Poll Finds
item.description: A vast majority of Americans favor requiring artificial intelligence companies to meet independent safety benchmarks for their models, even if those standards mean slowing development of the technology, according to a new poll. to establish guardrails for AI systems, with 81% indicating that safety should come before the pursuit of innovation, according to the poll released Wednesday by Quinnipiac University. In lieu of new federal rules, the executives agreed to voluntary measures that include third-party safety assessments of models and more stringent internal controls over their systems.

Funding to nuclear power-focused startups hit an all-time high this year, fueled by expectations of surging energy demand around artificial intelligence. Much of this year’s funding went to a few heavily financed nuclear startups.

item.title: The IPO Window Is Opening Selectively; Readiness Will Decide Who Gets Through
item.description: Public-market activity is returning selectively, led by companies that used the slower years to build scale and strengthen their financial and operating foundations. Collectively, venture-backed startups raised $110.8 billion through IPOs, compared with $12.6 billion a year earlier. For founders, late-stage startups and investors tracking exit readiness, the message is not simply to wait for a better market.

item.title: Generali’s aggregate reinsurance in focus as European cats and weather bite in 2026
item.description: Analysts at investment bank Jefferies have brought insurer Generali’s aggregate reinsurance protection into focus, saying that losses from catastrophes and weather events in Europe could drive the insurer to make reinsurance recoveries from its aggregate protection this year, given the restructuring of the coverage for 2026. Generali had restructured its aggregate reinsurance arrangement for the 2026 calendar year, to provide greater protection against frequency loss events. The Jefferies analyst team came away from its meeting with Generali’s management saying, given the loss run-rate in Europe from weather and catastrophes this year, “It seems likely that Generali will hit the aggregate reinsurance retention (unlike last year).”

item.title: Catastrophe bond market keeps record pace after above-average Q3: Report
item.description: Catastrophe bond issuance was above-average at $948 million for the third-quarter of the year which has served to keep the market on pace to set new records, with total nine-month 2026 issuance reaching a new $18.9 billion high of risk capital analysed and tracked by Artemis, our latest quarterly catastrophe bond market report shows . The Artemis Q3 2026 catastrophe bond and related insurance-linked securities (ILS) market report dissects an above-average $948 million issuance period for the sector following on from the record first-half. The Artemis Q3 2026 Catastrophe Bond Market Report, available to download now, examines cat bond and related insurance-linked securities (ILS) risk capital issued in the third-quarter of the year, key trends from the period and reviews nine month cat bond market activity .
